summary: Specifies forty-two cipher suites that let TLS use the Camellia block cipher. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: TLS can lock messages with different secret-code machines. This adds forty-two ways to use one called Camellia.

subtitle: New TLS cipher suites that bring the Camellia block cipher to CBC, GCM and pre-shared-key modes.

tldr.problem: TLS needed more cipher suites for the Camellia block cipher, covering SHA-2 hashes, Galois Counter Mode, elliptic curves and pre-shared keys. RFC 5932 only had Camellia suites with a SHA-256 based HMAC.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines eight HMAC-based CBC suites, twenty GCM suites and fourteen PSK suites, each with an assigned two-byte code in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry.
tldr.outcome: It gives TLS implementations more Camellia options, and says how the PRF is chosen for TLS 1.2 and earlier versions. It has since been updated by RFC 8996 and RFC 10015.

today: RFC 6367 is Informational and has been updated by RFC 8996 and RFC 10015. Check those documents before relying on these suites.

sections.title: Adding Camellia to TLS
sections.content:
RFC 5932 already specified Camellia cipher suites for TLS, with a SHA-256 based Hashed Message Authentication Code (HMAC) and asymmetric key encryption. RFC 6367 adds more suites so that Camellia can be used as a block cipher in TLS in further ways.

The new suites include variants with the SHA-2 family of hash functions and with Galois Counter Mode (GCM). Elliptic curve suites and pre-shared key (PSK) suites are also included.
sections.plainLanguage: TLS already knew one way to use the Camellia lock. This note teaches it many more ways to use the same lock.

sections.title: Three Families of Cipher Suites
sections.content:
The suites fall into three groups. The HMAC-based group has eight suites using Camellia in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a SHA-2 family HMAC and elliptic curve key exchange, such as TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_128_CBC_SHA256.

The GCM-based group has twenty suites. They use the same asymmetric algorithms plus RSA, DHE, DH and anonymous DH variants, with the authenticated encryption modes defined in TLS 1.2 and Camellia in GCM.

The PSK-based group has fourteen suites. The first six use Camellia with GCM and the next eight use Camellia with a SHA-2 family HMAC.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three boxes of locks. One box uses a chain of blocks, one uses a faster lock that also checks for tampering, and one uses a secret both sides already share.

sections.title: Key Sizes, Ciphers and Key Exchange
sections.content:
Key exchange for the RSA, DHE_RSA, DH_RSA, DHE_DSS, DH_DSS, ECDH, DH_anon and ECDHE suites is done as defined in RFC 5246.

The CAMELLIA_128_CBC suites use a 128-bit key and a 128-bit Initialization Vector (IV). The CAMELLIA_256_CBC suites use a 256-bit key and a 128-bit IV. CAMELLIA_128_GCM and CAMELLIA_256_GCM are defined following the AES GCM suites of RFC 5288, since AES and Camellia share key sizes and block length.

PSK suites are described by RFC 5487 for the SHA-256/384 variants and RFC 5489 for ECDHE_PSK.
sections.plainLanguage: The number 128 or 256 says how long the secret key is. A longer key is a bigger combination lock.

sections.title: Hashes and the PRF
sections.content:
For TLS 1.2, suites ending in _SHA256 use HMAC-SHA-256 as the MAC algorithm, and the pseudorandom function (PRF) is the TLS PRF with SHA-256. Suites ending in _SHA384 use HMAC-SHA-384 and the TLS PRF with SHA-384.

When the suites are used with TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1, the PRF is calculated as the specification of that version says.
sections.plainLanguage: The hash name at the end of a suite says which scrambling recipe the two sides use to make their keys and to check messages.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: At the time of writing, the RFC says there are no known weak keys for Camellia and no security problems with Camellia had been found, citing NESSIE, CRYPTREC and a paper in LNCS 5867. The security considerations of RFC 5116, RFC 5289 and RFC 5487 also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: When this was written, nobody had found a way to pick the Camellia lock, and the older safety notes still apply.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA allocated the suite numbers in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry. They run from {0xC0,0x72} to {0xC0,0x9B}, for example TLS_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_128_GCM_SHA256 is {0xC0,0x7A}. In section 2.3 the first PSK suite is printed with the code {0xC0,0x8D}, but the IANA list in section 5 gives it {0xC0,0x8E}, the value that follows the other GCM codes.
sections.plainLanguage: Each lock recipe gets its own two-part number so both sides can say which one they want.
